case_title: DR NARESH KUMAR MANGLA v. SMT. ANITA AGARWAL & ORS. ETC.
accused_socioeconomic_status: propertied and wealthy persons of influence
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B, s.498-A, s.323, s.506 and s.313; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3 and s.4
evidence_type: FIR, medical reports, call history, financial transactions
aggravating_circumstances: Demand for dowry, prior incidents of assault, unnatural death within seven years of marriage
neutral_facts: The accused, who are the in-laws of the deceased, were charged with the unnatural death of the deceased, who was a doctor. The FIR alleged that the deceased was pressurized to bring money and that the accused had assaulted her in 2017. The deceased was admitted to a hospital in a critical condition and later died. The accused were granted anticipatory bail by the High Court, but the Supreme Court overturned this decision, citing deficiencies in the investigation. The Court directed the CBI to conduct a further investigation into the case, noting that the investigation was inadequate and potentially biased.
